heading: Sports and physical activity interventions in autism spectrum disorder: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis
text: The study evaluates motor, social, executive, behavioural and psychosocial effects of sports interventions.
notProven: Variable methodological quality means broad benefits should not be promised across every area.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published 2019–2025. Variable methodological quality means broad benefits should not be promised across every area.

heading: Comparative efficacy of various physical activity interventions on individuals with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
text: The study indirectly compares different forms of physical activity.
notProven: Network rankings do not equal high certainty or an individual prescription.
linea: Systematic review and network meta-analysis. Network rankings do not equal high certainty or an individual prescription.

heading: Effects of exercise intervention on inhibitory control in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study finds a group-level signal of improvement in inhibitory control.
notProven: It does not show that exercise generally 'treats' executive-function difficulties in autism.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. It does not show that exercise generally 'treats' executive-function difficulties in autism.

heading: Effects of Physical Exercise on Motor Skills in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
text: The study specifically evaluates changes in motor skills after exercise.
notProven: Motor outcomes should not automatically be extrapolated to communication, behaviour or wellbeing.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs. Motor outcomes should not automatically be extrapolated to communication, behaviour or wellbeing.

heading: Exercise Interventions for Autistic People: An Integrative Review of Evidence from Clinical Trials
text: The study summarises signals of benefit in motor outcomes, sleep, executive function and some social/communication outcomes.
notProven: The evidence is more abundant in children than adults and varies greatly by intervention.
linea: Integrative review of trials. The evidence is more abundant in children than adults and varies greatly by intervention.

heading: School absenteeism among autistic children and adolescents: a scoping review
text: The study finds higher absenteeism in several datasets and relationships with mental health, other conditions, bullying and limited knowledge about autism.
notProven: Evidence on interventions to reduce absenteeism remains limited.
linea: Scoping review of 42 studies. Evidence on interventions to reduce absenteeism remains limited.

heading: Workplace accommodations and autism: a systematic review
text: The study identifies workplace adjustments and environmental factors that may be useful for autistic workers.
notProven: Samples are small and self-reported; evidence for the effectiveness of each adjustment remains limited.
linea: Systematic review of 10 empirical studies. Samples are small and self-reported; evidence for the effectiveness of each adjustment remains limited.

heading: Employment and the lived experience of autistic adults: a systematic synthesis
text: The study highlights environmental and social barriers in employment and the need to include autistic voices in the design of support.
notProven: It cannot quantify which adjustment works best or represent every employment sector.
linea: Systematic review/synthesis of 34 articles. It cannot quantify which adjustment works best or represent every employment sector.

heading: Support programs for autistic young adults in higher education: a systematic review
text: Mentoring appears as one of the most frequent and promising components of university support programmes.
notProven: Programmes are heterogeneous and the samples under-represent many autistic profiles.
linea: Systematic review of 16 studies. Programmes are heterogeneous and the samples under-represent many autistic profiles.

heading: Higher-education interventions for mental health and wellbeing of neurodivergent students: a systematic review
text: The literature is concentrated on ADHD and autism; there is little co-design and very little research on other neurotypes.
notProven: It does not show that one university programme is universally effective.
linea: Systematic review of 37 studies from 7 countries. It does not show that one university programme is universally effective.

heading: Gender identity, sexual orientation and adverse sexual experiences in autistic females: a cross-sectional study
text: The study describes group differences in gender identity/sexual orientation and adverse sexual experiences.
notProven: It cannot establish causation or represent the full diversity of experiences; the transgender subsample was small.
linea: Cross-sectional study with 295 participants (134 autistic, 161 non-autistic). It cannot establish causation or represent the full diversity of experiences; the transgender subsample was small.

heading: Prevalence of co-occurring mental health diagnoses in the autism population: a systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study documents frequent co-occurrence of several mental-health conditions in autistic people.
notProven: Heterogeneity exceeded 95% for many estimates; pooled figures should not be used as universal rates.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 100 eligible studies and 96 in meta-analysis. Heterogeneity exceeded 95% for many estimates; pooled figures should not be used as universal rates.

heading: A systematic meta-review of systematic reviews on attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
text: The study provides a broad synthesis of prevalence, associated factors, diagnosis and interventions in ADHD.
notProven: Many biological and social factors are correlational; association should not be translated into cause.
linea: Meta-review of 231 systematic reviews/meta-analyses. Many biological and social factors are correlational; association should not be translated into cause.

heading: Comparative efficacy and tolerability of medications for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder in children, adolescents, and adults: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
text: The study compares the efficacy and tolerability of ADHD medications across different age groups.
notProven: Comparative evidence is mainly short term; robust data at 26–52 weeks are lacking.
linea: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of 133 double-blind RCTs. Comparative evidence is mainly short term; robust data at 26–52 weeks are lacking.

heading: Effects of Pharmacological Treatment for ADHD on Quality of Life: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
text: The study specifically evaluates whether pharmacological treatment changes quality of life, not only symptoms.
notProven: Effects on quality of life are a different outcome from symptom reduction and depend on the scales and follow-up period used.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 17 RCTs and 5,388 participants. Effects on quality of life are a different outcome from symptom reduction and depend on the scales and follow-up period used.

heading: Pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions for adults with ADHD: systematic review and component network meta-analysis
design: Systematic review and component network meta-analysis
text: Stimulants and atomoxetine showed consistent efficacy for core symptoms across several sources of assessment; other interventions produced less consistent results.
notProven: Long-term research is insufficient, and effects of non-pharmacological interventions depend greatly on who rates the outcome.
linea: Systematic review and component network meta-analysis with 113 unique RCTs and 14,887 participants. Long-term research is insufficient, and effects of non-pharmacological interventions depend greatly on who rates the outcome.

heading: Predictors of Adult Psychiatric Outcomes of Childhood ADHD: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
text: The study analyses which childhood factors are associated with psychiatric outcomes in adulthood.
notProven: The studies have methodological limitations and predictors should not be presented as an individual's destiny.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 36 studies and 119 predictors. The studies have methodological limitations and predictors should not be presented as an individual's destiny.

heading: Miss. Diagnosis: A Systematic Review of ADHD in Adult Women
text: The study describes the impact of undiagnosed ADHD and adult diagnosis on wellbeing, relationships, sense of control and self-understanding in women.
notProven: The qualitative evidence base is small and does not define a universal female phenotype.
linea: Systematic review of 8 articles. The qualitative evidence base is small and does not define a universal female phenotype.

heading: Mapping the Landscape of ADHD Research in Girls and Women: A Scoping Review and Network Analysis
sample: Literature on ADHD in girls and women
text: The study maps which areas have been researched and where sex/gender-specific gaps remain.
notProven: A bibliometric map does not by itself demonstrate clinical differences.
linea: Scoping review and network analysis. A bibliometric map does not by itself demonstrate clinical differences.

heading: The effects of computerized executive function training on youth with ADHD: A systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study evaluates benefits and limitations of computerised programmes targeting executive function.
notProven: It should not be presented as a substitute for treatments with a more established evidence base; transfer to everyday life is a separate question.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. It should not be presented as a substitute for treatments with a more established evidence base; transfer to everyday life is a separate question.
